# API doc updates
<!-- Thank you for submitting a pull request to our repo. -->

<!-- If this is your first PR in the ASP.NET Core repo, please run through the checklist
below to ensure a smooth review and merge process for your PR. -->

- [X] You've read the [Contributor Guide](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) and [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/main/CODE-OF-CONDUCT.md).
- [X] You've included unit or integration tests for your change, where applicable.
- [X] You've included inline docs for your change, where applicable.
- [X] There's an open issue for the PR that you are making. If you'd like to propose a new feature or change, please open an issue to discuss the change or find an existing issue.

Many unrelated changes manually merged into one PR for reasons I fail to understand.

## Description
1. Descriptions for [status codes](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/microsoft.aspnetcore.http.statuscodes) are available from [GetReasonPhrase](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/microsoft.aspnetcore.webutilities.reasonphrases.getreasonphrase).
2. Be specific about what a [Stream](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/system.io.stream) required by a [StreamOutputFormatter](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/microsoft.aspnetcore.mvc.formatters.streamoutputformatter) is.
3. A standard [StringOutputFormatter](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/microsoft.aspnetcore.mvc.formatters.stringoutputformatter) can only format a `string` into media type `text/plain` encoded with [UTF8](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/system.text.encoding.utf8) or [Unicode](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/system.text.encoding.unicode).
4. Provide stand-alone documentation for `ExecuteResultAsync` in [PageResult](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/microsoft.aspnetcore.mvc.razorpages.pageresult).
5. Add a link to [StatusCodes](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/microsoft.aspnetcore.http.statuscodes) to the description of [ContentResult.StatusCode](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/microsoft.aspnetcore.mvc.contentresult.statuscode#definition).
6. Add a link to [ResponseHeaders.ContentType](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/microsoft.aspnetcore.http.headers.responseheaders.contenttype) to the description of [ContentResult.ContentType](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/microsoft.aspnetcore.mvc.contentresult.contenttype#definition).
7. Mention that the magic directory of `DisplayTemplates` should be placed under [Pages](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/aspnet/core/tutorials/razor-pages/razor-pages-start#pages-folder-2).
8. Explain how to find the [template name](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/microsoft.aspnetcore.mvc.modelbinding.modelmetadata.templatehint) in the model metadata.
9. Explain how to specify a [template hint](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/microsoft.aspnetcore.mvc.modelbinding.modelmetadata.templatehint) in the model metadata.

Fixes #38833

issue_context.title: StatusCodes: improve documentation
issue_context.body:
<!--

More information on our issue management policies can be found here: https://aka.ms/aspnet/issue-policies

-->

### Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.
I am trying to provide a textual representation of a HTTP status code—but the definition of [StatusCodes](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/microsoft.aspnetcore.http.statuscodes) is one way only.

### Describe the solution you'd like
The documentation for [Status404NotFound](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/microsoft.aspnetcore.http.statuscodes.status404notfound) should say:

> The numeric value of [NotFound](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/system.net.httpstatuscode?view=net-6.0#System_Net_HttpStatusCode_NotFound).

### Additional context
That way, the reader can discover that there *is* an enum for HTTP status codes, which is exactly what is needed to have a two-way mapping, and understand what these status codes really mean without leaving the documentation portal.

Fixed by #38831.
comments:
What is the two way mapping is for? Do you mean you're trying to programmatically display status codes as text, as well as reverse lookup by text back to integers?  Have you tried the ReasonPhrases class?
https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/bf9225b8d7fd5f8ee855dd50407a90587b812662/src/Http/WebUtilities/src/ReasonPhrases.cs#L90

> and understand what these status codes really mean without leaving the documentation portal.

The current comment for Status404NotFound reads: `HTTP status code 404.` I could see expanding that to something like `HTTP status code 404, meaning the resource wasn't found.`

This issue will be closed automatically in 7 days if we do not hear back from you by then - please feel free to re-open it if you come back to this issue after that time.

review_comments: I'm hesitant to use `<see href=...` in a bunch of places since it breaks the summary in intellisense. See https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/pull/38659#discussion_r760672551
I thought it would be broken when the link is relative?
I wasn't able to reproduce this issue, the href worked fine for me locally in VS 2022.

Do you plan to include the description in each constant's `<summary>` like @Tratcher suggested in https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/38833#issuecomment-987033883? That seems like it could be helpful.

It would be more helpful is to refer to the documentation of [HttpStatusCode](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/system.net.httpstatuscode) because 1DR > NIH.  But then, why not borrow the values defined in the system library?  I do not get that rejection at all.

What's 1DR?

API cross references should be limited to APIs that will be directly used together. StatusCodes and HttpStatusCodes won't be used together. It's better for each of them to reference something authoritative like an RFC.

1DR is the one definition rule.  According to this rule, [StatusCodes](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/microsoft.aspnetcore.http.statuscodes), defined a dependent library, is secondary to [HttpStatusCode](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/system.net.httpstatuscode), defined in the base library, and should import the values defined there rather than rolling its own (NIH).  It does not imply that [HttpStatusCode](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/system.net.httpstatuscode) should be used alongside [StatusCodes](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/microsoft.aspnetcore.http.statuscodes); just the opposite, except in the definition of the latter (or where you need a true `enum` for some reason, which may also happen). And the documentation of the dependent library, again by 1DR, should reference the documentation of the base library, except for bogus values that are not defined there.
